sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 11-07-2022 at about 10.00 p.m., the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HM-9751 and his friend was riding the same carefully and they reached at Batawadi 'Y' Junction, opposite to Mirchi Petrol Bunk, Tumkur Town, 80 feet road,
NH-206 road, Tumkuru, and by switching on the right indicator taking right turn, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-19-F-3524 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) drove the same with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the accident, rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Petitioner was immediately taken to District Govt. Hospital, Tumkur, wherein the doctor referred him to Srinivasa hospital, wherein after first aid, he was referred to Nimhans hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, the petitioner was shifted to Basavanagudi Medical Centre, Bengaluru, wherein he was taken treatment as an inpatient.
Then shifted to Siddaganga hospital, Tumkur, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that Petitioner has spent Rs.30,00,000/- for treatment,
medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 23 years,
working in a private firm and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent has appeared before the court and filed the objections denying the negligence of its driver.

It has contended that the offending bus was in its schedule trip from Bengaluru towards Tumkuru, the driver of the said bus driving slowly and carefully and alleged that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle, without wearing helmet, without observing main road vehicles, came from opposite road and took right turn, lost control over the vehicle and fell down, and rider of motorcycle was responsible for the accident.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the owner and insurer of motorcycle were not arrayed as respondents in the petition.
It has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, treatment taken by him, disability suffered by him and also the expenses claimed by the Petitioner and prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was a pillion rider in motorcycle bearing No. KA-06-HM- 9751 on 11-07-2022, about 10.00 p.m., at Batawadi 'Y' Junction, Opp.Mirchi Petrol Bunk, Tumkur Town & District only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-19-F-3524?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?

sentences.text: 3. What order ?

5. In order to prove the claim, the mother of Petitioner examined as PW.1 and in support of his case,
3 witnesses are examined as PW-2 to 4 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.34.

6. The driver of offending vehicle is examined as RW-1 and one document is marked at Ex.R.1.
7.

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 8.
ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 11-07-2022 at about 10.00 p.m., he was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HM-9751 and his friend was riding the same carefully and they reached at Batawadi 'Y' Junction, opposite to Mirchi Petrol Bunk,
Tumkur Town, 80 feet road, NH-206 road, Tumkuru, and by switching on the right indicator taking right turn, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-19-F-3524 drove the same with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.

Due to the accident,
rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

9. In order to substantiate his case, mother of the petitioner was examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 9, 11 and 12 i.e.FIR, complaint, crime details form, vehicle seizure mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, notice, reply, indemnity bond, RC, FC, charge sheet and order sheet in AIR Misc.229/2022.
To support the case of the petitioner, the rider of the motorcycle and eye witness to the incident and attender were examined as PW3 and PW4.
They have reiterated the averments and of the petition.

Though the learned counsel for the Respondent has cross examined PW1 and 3 at length, nothing have been elicited to disprove the version of the petitioner and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
10. The driver of the offending vehicle was examined as RW1 and he has produced his authorization letter at EX.R1.He has deposed
that the accident occurred due to negligence of the rider of the two wheeler.

The rider of the motor vehicle without following the traffic rules and regulation and without observing the vehicle, took turn towards right side and lost control over two wheeler and thereby fell down on road, touched to left back side of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Both the rider and pillion rider were not wearing helmets at time of accident.

On the other hand, the respondent has contended that the investigation officer without conducting proper investigation, in active collusion with the petitioner, has filed false charge sheet against the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent has vehemently argued that the petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
The petitioner in active collusion with the police have got created the police documents and offending vehicle was falsely implicated in order to get compensation to the petitioner from this court.
He further argued that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle and not on the part of offending vehicle.
Thereby the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

The sketch shows that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, hence, the rider is responsible to the extent of 50% by way of contributory negligence and relied upon the following decisions:
1) 1994 ACJ 1303 between Mataji Bewa and others Vs Hemanta Kumar Jena and another.
2) MFA no 3459/2021 between Sadath Ali Khan V Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another 3)ILR 2003 KAR 409 between P Varalakshmi reddy and others V the Karnataka state Road Transport Corporation 4) MFA 1749/2023 between the Divisional Manager Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation V Mahadevaiah M and others 5) MFA 2921/2012 between Smt Vijayalakshmi K N V Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation 12.
On perusal of police and medical records and material available on record it appears that regarding accident and petitioner sustained injuries in a RTA are in dispute.

13. Keeping in view of the material available on record, let us discuss whether the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle or the accident occurred when the rider of the two wheeler rode in a rash or negligent manner and dashed to left front side of the offending vehicle.
The police records show that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle the accident was caused.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

14. During the course of the cross-examination of PW1, the learned counsel for the respondent has put forth the suggestion that at time of the accident the rider and her son were not wearing the helmets.
She denied the same.
She also denied that near petrol bunk the rider of the motorcycle suddenly took turn from left side to right side and dashed against the back side of the offending vehicle.
Further she denied that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motor vehicle and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Except these suggestions the Respondent has not proved the said fact by examining any witness to support its contention as offending vehicle was not caused any accident.
The EX.P6 IMV report shows that the offending vehicle sustained damages on front left side corner bumper and head light.
Material available on record shows that the offending vehicle hit left portion of the motor cycle.

Therefore the contention of the respondent that near petrol bunk the rider of the motorcycle suddenly took turn from left side to right side and dashed to the back side of the offending vehicle is not tenable.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that the driver of the offending vehicle has not disputed regarding the alleged accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.

There is no material before this court to show that at the time of accident the petitioner was not wearing helmet and the accident occurred,
due to the negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle and not on the part of driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, with due respect of above decisions the facts and circumstances are not squarely applicable to this case.
16. There are no materials on record to disprove the PW-1 evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborate with the documents produced by PW1.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

17. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.5 wound certificate and material available on record, the petitioner has sustained left ear bleeding with head injury - CT brain revealed left extradural hematoma, left temporal bone fracture and left zygoma fracture.
Doctor opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
18. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to District Govt. hospital, Tumkuru, wherein, the doctors referred him to Srinivasa hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and he had a GCS of E3V3M5.
Thereafter he was admitted in Nimhans hospital.

19. PW-2 Dr.Sahilsh A.V.Rao, consultant neuro surgeon at Padmashree Diagnostic, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated as an inpatient at various hospitals in Bengaluru and Petitioner has sustained left fronto temporo parietal extradural and sub dural hematoma with overlying fracture of bone and he underwent left fronto temporo parietal craniotomy and evacuation of hematoma.
PW-2 has stated that the petitioner has also underwent lumbar drain placement.
Further, bifrontal de-compressive craniectomy along with duroplasty.
He was on mechanical ventilator with a GCS of E1VtM2.

Later petitioner was admitted and taken treatment in Basavanagudi medical centre, Bengaluru, Siddaganga hospital, Tumkuru, Aster R.V.hospital, Bengaluru, wherein underwent cranioplasty using 3D printed Mesh and for closure of tracheostomy wound.

PW-2 has stated that now the Petitioner is unable to stand, walk without support, impaired memory, slurred speech along with behavioral disturbances, he is verbally abusive, his left eye vision is impaired, impaired memory and impaired intelligence and he was laughing inappropriately, had spasticity in all 4 limbs with weakness.
20. PW-2 further submitted that he has done neuro psychological assessment on 24-08-2024, the petitioner IQ was 66 (normal range 90-109).
PW-2 has stated that he is below average in thinking and reasoning, he has mild mental retardation.
His frontal and parietal lobes were inadequate in functioning.
He obtained an IDEAS score of 10 suggestive of 40-70% moderate disability.

sentences.text: On examination he has assessed the total disability of around 61%.
This disability pertaining to whole body and is likely to be permanent.
21. PW-2 in his cross-examination has stated that he has not treated the Petitioner.
Nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW2 to disbelieve his evidence.
22. It is pertinent to note that medical documents, it show that the petitioner sustained left extradural hematoma, left temporal bone fracture and left zygoma fracture.
23. PW-2 doctor has assessed the physical disability at 61% for whole body.
He has not treated the petitioner at any point of time.

Considering head injury sustained by the petitioner as mentioned in the wound certificate and medical documents and considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-2 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 50%.
24. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 23 years and in the wound certificate and other medical record it was mentioned age of the petitioner as 25 years.

Wherein Ex.P.17 Aadhar card shows that he was born on 15-01-1999, the same is considered as age of the deceased as on the date of accident as 24 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
25.
The age of the petitioner is 24 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted and treated in various hospitals.
PW-1 has stated that at the time of accident, the petitioner was working in a private firm and was earning Rs.35,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, PW-1 has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
26. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs.15,500/- Per Month.
Since the functional disability is 50%, future prospects of 40% of income is added to it.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
27. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner was a working in a private firm, considering nature of injuries and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 50%.
28.
The petitioner was aged about 24 years as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18.

The notional income taken as Rs 15,500+40%=21,700 x 12 x 18 x 50/100= Rs.23,43,600/-
towards loss of future income.
29. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained head injuries and was inpatient for a period of Hari Prasad M.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134284684/
6 52 days and he is still unconscious, which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .1,00,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.

sentences.text: 30. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .50,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
31. Medical expenses:

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the PW-1 has produced medical bills at Ex.P.13 amounting to 40,58,911/- and the medical bills at Ex.P.34 amounting to Rs.18,775/-.
32.
The receipt i.e., (sl.no. 141, 142, 169,305 to 308, 320 to 322 and 391 and 392 )receipts issued by the hospital towards the advance payment and same part and parcel of the final bills.
Hence, the receipts (sl.no. 141, 142, 169, 305 to 308, 320 to 322 and 391 and 392 ) are not considered as they are included in final bill.

The inpatient settlement receipt bearing No.IP24CA24114420 (sl.no.422)
for payment of Rs.77,229/- is not considered as it is included in serial no 393 bill receipt no IP23145.
33.
The actual medical expenses incurred by the petitioner after deduction of advance bills and repeated is only Rs 34,75,279.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of 34,75,279/- towards Medical Expenses.
34. Conveyance, food and nourishment charges:

Initially he was treated at Sreenivasa hospital,
Bengaluru from 11-7-2022 to 14-07-2022.

Ex.P.14- Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru from 15-07-2022 to 19-07-2022, he was treated at Basavanagudi Medical Centre, Bengaluru, from 19-07- 2022 to 29-8-2022, he was treated as an inpatient at Siddaganga hospital, Tumkur, from 29-8-2022 to 21- 09-2022, he was treated as an inpatient at Aster RV hospital, Bengaluru, from 01-02-2023 to 06-02-2023, again from 27-07-2023 to 30-07-2023 i.e, totally for a period of 52 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .60,000/- under the head of conveyance, food and nourishment charges.
35. Loss of marriage prospects and disfiguration:
Ex.P.15 are the photographs.
According to these photographs Petitioner's condition is pathetic.
Due to head injury, Petitioner has suffered disfiguration on his face and he has lost marriage prospects and he might not get bride.
Considering these two aspects, Petitioner is awarded compensation of .2,00,000/- towards loss of marriage prospects and disfiguration.
36. Loss of earning during laid up period: With regard to loss of earnings during treatment.

Ex.P.14- Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at NIMHANS hospital,
Bengaluru from 15-07-2022 to 19-07-2022, he was treated at Basavanagudi Medical Centre,
Bengaluru, from 19-07- 2022 to 29-8-2022, he was treated as an inpatient at Siddaganga hospital,

He was admitted in the hospital multiple times and was undergoing treatment nearly for one year and hence loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 1 year.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .1,60,000/-.
37.
Attendant charges:
the material available on record shows that the Petitioner has lost his job and lying on bed in a vegetative state.
By considering the present condition of the Petitioner, the attender or a care taker is required to look after the petitioner.
PW 4 being an attender has stated that the parents of the petitioner have appointed him as servant to take care of the petitioner and his salary is Rs.15,000/-.Considering all these
, Petitioner is awarded attendant charges from the date of accident till date @10,000/-p.m.

The total attendant charges will be 10,000 x 25 = 2,50,000/-.

ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.66,38,879/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 75% amount shall be disbursed to the natural guardian of the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and remaining 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The EX.P6 IMV report shows that the offending vehicle sustained damages on front left side corner bumper and head light.
Material available on record shows that the offending vehicle hit left portion of the motor cycle.
Therefore the contention of the respondent that near petrol bunk the rider of the motorcycle suddenly took turn from left side to right side and dashed to the back side of the offending vehicle is not tenable.

4 15.
It is pertinent to note that the driver of the offending vehicle has not disputed regarding the alleged accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.
There is no material before this court to show that at the time of accident the petitioner was not wearing helmet and the accident occurred,
due to the negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle and not on the part of driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, with due respect of above decisions the facts and circumstances are not squarely applicable to this case.
16. There are no materials on record to disprove the PW-1 evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborate with the documents produced by PW1.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
26. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs.15,500/- Per Month.
Since the functional disability is 50%, future prospects of 40% of income is added to it.
Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
27. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
